requirement: In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.
rationale:
**Determination: true.** The `{impl}` code covers every obligation in `requirements.references.book_badges`, and the tests cover the main points of the design space. The CSS obligations have no tests; I judged that acceptable.

**Reference badges.**
- `replace_references` (src/lib.rs:381) turns each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}` or `{test}` role into `<a class="habeas-req-badge habeas-req-ref-KIND" href=…>` wrapping a Shields.io image.
- `shield_badge` (src/lib.rs:441) builds a static `img.shields.io/badge/<label>-<message>-<color>` URL. The alt text is `"<role> <full name>"`, so it shows both the role and the full name.
- `ReferenceKind::label` and `ReferenceKind::color` supply the role text and colour.
- The link target is built by `chapter_href(current_path, target.path, anchor)`, using the anchor from `DefinitionKind::anchor`. That produces the cross-chapter, relative links the requirement asks for.
- References to unknown names are left literal.

**Definition badges.**
- `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs:282) renders each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive as a Shields.io badge. `DefinitionKind::badge` gives the kind text, "req" or "example", and the badge carries the anchor id.
- Invalid or unclosed directives, and everything outside a directive, are copied through unchanged, so that text stays literal.
- The "See evidence" link and the wrapping detail-page link are specified by `requirements.index.navigation`, which the same function also marks with `{impl}`.
- The `{term}` branch of `replace_references` is covered by `requirements.definitions.references`, also marked on that function.

**Styling.** `md/habeas.css` is anchored as an `{impl}` of the requirement (md/requirements/references.md).
- `a.habeas-req-badge:visited` keeps `color: inherit` and `text-decoration: none`, and the text is inside an image anyway, so it stays legible after a visit.
- `a.habeas-req-badge:focus-visible` draws a 2px outline, which is the visible keyboard-focus indicator.
- `a.habeas-req-badge:hover` applies `filter: brightness(1.08)`, which the requirement allows with MAY.
- The remaining rules lay out the badges and are badge-only.
- `book.toml` loads the stylesheet through `additional-css`.

**Tests.**
- `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` (src/lib.rs:1143) renders all three roles from `guides/deep.md`. It checks the class, the `../requirements.html#habeas-req-…` link, and the Shields URL with the role and colour.
- `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` (src/lib.rs:1301) checks the example definition badge and its alt text, and that a `{test}` reference to an example links to `#habeas-example-…`. It also checks that invalid and code-fenced directives stay literal.
- `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` (src/lib.rs:1227) checks that text outside a directive stays literal.
- `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` (src/lib.rs:1129) checks the badge URL form and the alt text.

**Gaps.** There is no automated test for the CSS focus, hover or visited behaviour. These are small declarative rules and a visual browser check would be impractical here, so I accept that. Invalid-reference literalness is exercised only indirectly, by the invalid-namespace test, which is cited for `requirements.ci.identifiers`.

Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references: discovery MUST skip `.git` and `target` directories at any depth and the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories.
